title: The Battle of Hastings
description: October 1066. William of Normandy's invasion army faces King Harold's Anglo-Saxon shield wall on Senlac Hill. The player commands the Norman force and must break the shield wall through feigned retreats and combined cavalry-archer assaults before nightfall ends the battle.

anachronisms_found: Player Two's Anglo-Saxon leader is a generic KING unit rather than a named hero; the engine offers no Harold Godwinson, so this is defensible, but Harold is textually named while being represented by an anonymous monarch figure

Full economic/military infrastructure (TOWN_CENTER, BARRACKS, STABLE, ARCHERY_RANGE, BLACKSMITH, MONASTERY) for both sides on a one-day pitched battlefield near Hastings; neither army had settlements or production facilities on Senlac ridge (William's only fixed work was the motte at Hastings, miles away)
GOLD_MINE x5 and STONE_MINE x4 plus forage bushes and livestock as harvestable resources on what should be a purely tactical battlefield map
'Norman Reinforcements' trigger creating fresh riders 'from the coast' — William committed his whole force; no reinforcement column arrived during the battle
2560 oak trees on a 120x120 map produces a heavily forested field, whereas Senlac was an open ridge with cultivated slopes and only marshy ground and scattered woodland (the Malfosse) at the flanks
